Definition: from G1249; to be an attendant, i.e. wait upon (menially or as a host, friend, or (figuratively) teacher); technically, to act as a Christian deacon:--(ad-)minister (unto), serve, use the office of a deacon.
BiblicalUsage: To serve is to wait on others, and the word runs from the table to the cross. The Son of Man came not to be ministered unto but to minister, the apostles say it is not right to leave the word of God and serve tables, and Jesus promises that where He is, there shall His servant be.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe serving is the shape of greatness in the kingdom. Christ did not come to be waited on but to wait on us, and every table I serve, every need I meet, is a share in His own work.
